chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We have been narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said:
He (peace be upon him) said: 'They speak the truth.' I said: 'And how is it that his prayer is not counted for forty mornings, neither less than that nor more?'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, measured the creation of man, so He made it a nutfah (drop) for forty days. Then He transferred it and made it an 'alaqah (clot) for forty days. Then He transferred it and made it a mudghah (lump) for forty days.'
So when he drinks wine, it remains in his bone marrow (mushash) for forty days, according to the measure of the transition of his creation.'
He said, then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And similarly, all of his nourishment, his eating and drinking, remains in his bone marrow for forty days.'
ai.seo_question: Why are prayers not counted for forty days after drinking wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical rationale behind the forty-day period during which prayers are not accepted for one who consumes wine. He draws a profound parallel between the spiritual impurity caused by wine and the physical stages of human embryonic development, noting that the substance's essence lingers in the bone marrow (*mushash*) for forty days, mirroring the three forty-day phases of creation described in the Quran. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that physical consumption directly impacts the spiritual receptivity of the body, linking physiological reality with ritual validity.
